question: Does the complete publisher-hosted 2009 Silliman Journal article resolve site scope and whether its Nueva Ecija survey is independent from the 2006 NAST proceedings abstract?

access.retrievalMethod: The publisher-hosted article PDF was parsed and reviewed through the browser's document text view. The article download route was unavailable to the local command-line fetch during this pass, and PDF page screenshots did not load. No full local PDF or extracted-text copy was retained.
access.reviewedSections: Article metadata and abstract; methods; site list and sampling design; Nueva Ecija endemic/indigenous and introduced fish discussion/tables; Pampanga/Candaba aggregate fish discussion/tables; relevant conclusion and source-era diet discussion.
access.textLayerLimit: The PDF text layer exposes the five-column Nueva Ecija table values but does not preserve all cell positions reliably. No complete row-to-waterbody matrix or SIV values were transcribed; the printed table layout still needs visual verification.

publicationMetadata.citation: Paz-Alberto, A. M., Castro, E. S., Flores, V. L., & Romero, M. A. V. (2009). Endemic, Indigenous, and Introduced Species in the Freshwater Ecosystems of Nueva Ecija and Pampanga: Status, Diversity, and Impacts. Silliman Journal, 50(2), 43-60.
publicationMetadata.dateInterpretation: The issue and article itself identify the publication as 2009; the OJS page's later Published field does not establish a 2022 field survey or dataset.

methodsAsReported.nuevaEcija: Three designated stations per study area and ten randomly selected 10 m by 12 m quadrats per station.
methodsAsReported.organisms: Survey, collection, identification, description, classification and observation of mollusks, crustaceans, fishes and macroflora.
identificationReferences: Invasive Aquatic Animals in the Philippines, Guerrero (2002)
methodsAsReported.authenticationAsReported: The article says fisheries technologists at CLSU's Freshwater Aquaculture Center, NFRDI, and a National Museum Zoology Division taxonomist authenticated the identifications.
methodsAsReported.fishFieldDates: No fish-sampling dates were identified in the reviewed full-text sections.

waterbodyAssignmentLimits: The article names the Nueva Ecija and Pampanga study areas, but its text-extracted tables do not reliably preserve every species row's site-column alignment.
The Pampanga/Candaba species tables explicitly aggregate Candaba Swamp and Pampanga River; taxa are not separated among Apalit, San Simon, San Luis, and Candaba stations.
No station coordinates, vouchers, accession numbers, or specimen-level records were located in the reviewed sections.

sourceReportedFishFindings.explicitNuevaEcijaSiteStatement: The discussion explicitly reports Leiopotherapon plumbeus at Pampanga River in Palayan City, Paitan Lake, and Pantabangan Dam. It is an author-reported historical association, not a present-day occurrence.
sourceReportedFishFindings.talaveraHistoricalStatement: The article reports that no endemic/indigenous species were found in the surveyed Talavera River area while introduced species were reported there. This is a bounded historical study result, not an absence claim for other dates or the whole river.
sourceReportedFishFindings.introducedFishTableScope: Table 3 headings name the five Nueva Ecija waters. The text layer shows five nonblank SIV values for Oreochromis niloticus, but the table's cell positions were not visually verified; retain this as a table-structure lead rather than a finalized five-water occurrence matrix.
sourceReportedFishFindings.pampangaCandabaFishScope: The article reports six native/endemic fish names and nine introduced fish names across the combined Candaba Swamp and Pampanga River study scope. No fish taxon is assigned to an individual Pampanga reach or to Candaba alone in the reviewed tables.
sourceReportedFishFindings.pampangaCandabaIdentityConflict: The narrative's introduced-fish list names Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus, while Table 5's extracted row names Hypostomus plecostomus. Preserve the conflict; do not normalize either as a confirmed specimen identity.

overlap: Three authors overlap: Paz-Alberto, Castro, and Flores.
Both sources name the same five Nueva Ecija waters.
Both describe three stations and ten 10 m by 12 m quadrats per Nueva Ecija study area.
Both discuss Leiopotherapon plumbeus, Glossogobius giuris, and introduced tilapia from the Nueva Ecija survey scope.
relationshipToNast2006.expanded2009Scope: The 2009 article adds Pampanga River reaches at Apalit, San Simon and San Luis, and Candaba Swamp.
relationshipToNast2006.lineageDecision: The shared authors, exact five-water overlap, matching Nueva Ecija methods, and repeated fish-name leads indicate a close study lineage. Neither reviewed source establishes that the 2006 abstract and 2009 article are independent field datasets or provides collection dates that could resolve reuse/reanalysis. Do not sum totals or count them as independent survey confirmations.

rightsAssessment.publisherIssueTerms: The official issue states that copyright is held by the individual authors and Silliman Journal and that all rights are reserved. No item-specific open license or reuse permission was found.
rightsAssessment.contentDisposition: Keep brief attributed source summaries for research triage. Do not reproduce article text, tables, figures, SIV values, photographs, or table-derived app rows without a verified rights basis.

nextActions: Visually verify the full Nueva Ecija table column layout using a successfully accessible page image or an author-provided lawful copy before creating any complete site-by-site candidate matrix.
Look for the underlying 2005 CLSU report, field log, or author-supported dataset to establish collection dates and whether the 2006 NAST and 2009 Silliman records reuse the same field sample.
Keep all historical fish leads research-only until source-level taxonomy, locality, rights, currentness and independent evidence are separately reviewed.

sources.supports: Official publisher metadata, abstract, article issue information and OJS Published field.
Official full-text PDF text view for the article's methods, site names, fish discussion, tables, and conclusion.
Official issue copyright and all-rights-reserved notice.
The related 2006 proceedings abstract; used only for study-lineage comparison, not as independent confirmation.
